steve-jobs.structure_variant: The comeback that took a decade

shorts.hook: His own CEO told Wall Street he'd never work there again.
shorts.proof: Sept 1985: Sculley tells analysts there is no role for Steve Jobs at Apple, today or in the future. Jobs is 30.

shorts.hook: He lost money for ten straight years, then became a billionaire in a day.
shorts.proof: NeXT lost $40–66M a year; Pixar burned through about $50M of his own money. Then Toy Story, and a first day of trading from $22 to $39.

shorts.hook: Michael Dell said: shut Apple down.
shorts.proof: Oct 1997, Apple has just lost $1.05 billion. One year later: the iMac, and a $309 million profit.

steve-jobs.cold_open: In 1985, at thirty, Steve Jobs was pushed out of the company he started. Eleven years later, Apple bought his company for around $400 million, and got him back. This is how.
steve-jobs.dyegu_rule: Sometimes losing the version of your life you outgrew is how you build the one that lasts. Jobs didn't come back as the man who was fired. He came back ready. That's the DYEGU rule.
steve-jobs.comment_prompt: Tell me in the comments: which part of his exile speaks to your life?
steve-jobs.signoff: If stories like this help you keep going, subscribe. Until the next story... don't you ever give up.

featured_claims.text: Jobs and Steve Wozniak started Apple in Jobs's parents' garage when Jobs was 20
In April 1985 Sculley told the board he would resign unless Jobs was removed as head of the Macintosh division; the board backed Sculley
At the end of May 1985 Jobs was stripped of every operating role; he kept only the title of chairman
In September 1985 Jobs resigned as chairman, saying the board had made his plans "a very hostile situation"
He founded NeXT after leaving Apple in 1985

In February 1986 Jobs paid Lucasfilm $5 million for the graphics group's technology and put another $5 million into the new company, Pixar; Ed Catmull ran it day to day; its first product was a high-end image computer for medical imaging and film effects
Over the following years Jobs put about $50 million of his own money into Pixar
NeXT's computers struggled to find a market and NeXT stopped making its own hardware
Toy Story, the first computer-animated feature film, opened on 22 Nov 1995 and became the year's top-grossing film
Pixar went public on 29 Nov 1995 at $22 a share and closed its first day at $39; Jobs owned about 80%, which made him a billionaire
On 20 Dec 1996 Apple announced it would buy NeXT, a deal first announced at $400 million; it closed on 7 Feb 1997 at roughly $427–429 million in cash and stock
Jobs came back as an adviser to CEO Gil Amelio

shorts.hook: Twelve publishers said no. An eight-year-old said yes.
shorts.proof: Bloomsbury's chairman gave chapter one to his daughter Alice. An hour later she came downstairs asking for more.

shorts.hook: The first print run of Harry Potter: 500 copies.
shorts.proof: Three years earlier its author was on income support in Edinburgh, "as poor as it is possible to be in modern Britain."
A single mother on benefits a few years earlier, she heard Scholastic had won the US rights for $105,000.

jk-rowling.cold_open: In 1994, Joanne Rowling was a single mother on state benefits in Edinburgh, by her own account the biggest failure she knew. Then an eight-year-old girl read chapter one.
jk-rowling.dyegu_rule: Rock bottom strips away everything you were pretending to be. What's left is what you build on. Jo Rowling had one unfinished book and a baby asleep in a buggy. She built on that. That's the DYEGU rule.
jk-rowling.comment_prompt: Tell me in the comments: what's the one thing you'd still build on, even at your lowest?
jk-rowling.signoff: If stories like this help you keep going, subscribe. Until the next story... don't you ever give up.

featured_claims.text: Joanne Rowling was born on 31 July 1965 in Yate, England
In 1990 the idea for Harry Potter came to her on a delayed train; she was stuck for about four hours with nothing to write on
She was an Exeter University graduate working in London, including for Amnesty International, when she started the books
Her mother, Anne, had multiple sclerosis and died in 1990, aged 45
She moved to northern Portugal to teach English (afternoons and evenings, writing in the mornings), married Jorge Arantes in 1992 and had a daughter, Jessica, in 1993
She arrived with the first three chapters of Harry Potter
Harvard, 5 Jun 2008: seven years after graduating, her short marriage "had imploded"; she was jobless, a lone parent, and "as poor as it is possible to be in modern Britain, without being homeless"
She has said: "Depression is the most unpleasant thing I have ever experienced"
She wrote much of the first book in Edinburgh cafés
The Christopher Little Literary Agency took her on after a reader there liked the first three chapters
Little took about a year to find a publisher; the manuscript was turned down by twelve publishers (the widely reported figure; she has never named them)
Bloomsbury chairman Nigel Newton took the sample home and gave it to his eight-year-old daughter, Alice, who came back about an hour later asking for more

shorts.hook: He bet his entire $12,000 savings on one play.
shorts.proof: He expected 1,200 people. About 30 came. He lost his apartment.

shorts.hook: Six foot five. Living in a Geo Metro.
shorts.proof: Three months in that car, hiding it from the repo man, while the same play failed every year.

shorts.hook: He bought 330 acres of an army base.
shorts.proof: $30 million in 2015, about $250 million invested, 12 soundstages. Warner Bros.' lot is 110 acres.

tyler-perry.cold_open: In 1992, Tyler Perry spent his entire life savings on one play. About thirty people came. Twenty-three years later, he bought three hundred and thirty acres of Atlanta.
tyler-perry.dyegu_rule: He didn't change the dream. He changed how long he was willing to chase it, and he kept learning while he chased it. Six years of the same play failing, then year seven. That's the DYEGU rule.
tyler-perry.comment_prompt: Tell me in the comments: what are you on year three of right now?
tyler-perry.signoff: If stories like this help you keep going, subscribe. Until the next story... don't you ever give up.

featured_claims.text: Tyler Perry was born in 1969 and grew up in New Orleans
His mother grew up in the Jim Crow South; he has described growing up with an abusive, alcoholic father in an area marked by poverty, and credits his mother, aunts and grandmother
He moved to Atlanta to launch the play
Over those years he was homeless on and off, including living in a pay-by-the-week hotel
He created Madea (played by Perry himself in drag) in the 2000 play I Can Do Bad All by Myself
Madea's Family Reunion opened at No. 1 with $30.3 million in February 2006
In 2015 he bought 330 acres of the former Fort McPherson army post (488 acres in all) for $30 million
Part of that land was once used as a Confederate army base

He estimated his total investment at about $250 million; the lot has 12 soundstages and about 200 acres of green space, including historic homes on the old officers' row and a full-scale White House set
For comparison, Warner Bros.' Burbank studio lot is about 110 acres
The studio's grand opening gala was on 5 Oct 2019
Forbes estimated him a billionaire in 2020
